To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the band anticrossings in dilute group-II-oxides are strongly affected by the host material and that the coupling parameter increases with the electronegative difference between the anion and the oxygen.

(1) the band anticrossings are observed in ZnSO, ZnCdTeO, ZnSeO and ZnTeO, (2) the band anticcrossings are stronger in ZnTeO than ZnSO, and (3) the band anticrosings can be tuned by changing the host material.

the band anticrossings between the conduction-band edge and O energy levels are stronger in ZnTeO and ZnCdTe than ZnSeO and ZnSO and that the strength of these band anticrossings is approximately linear with the electronegative difference between the host and O anions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical properties of the dilute-oxide semiconductors ZnSO, ZnCdTeO, and CdTeO, which are grown by molecular beam epitaxy.
the optical properties of dilute group II–VI oxides.
the study of the electronic and structural properties of dilute group II-IV oxides.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the coupling parameter is determined by the electronegative difference between the host anion and O, but the energy separation between O and the conduction band is determined by the band gap and the band gap bowing parameter of the host semiconductor.

the band anticrossings are very similar in all four material systems and that the coupling parameters are very well explained by the electronegative differences between O and the different group II-VI anions.
a semiconductor matrix has no effect on the band anticcrossing interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the band anticrossed energy gap is not determined by a single parameter but rather by the coupling parameter and the energy separation between conduction band edge of the host and the O level.
